title: Travel
description: Ten short stories about travel in the United States and Canada: planning a trip, flying, trains, hotels and visiting cities.

lessons.title: Emma Plans a Trip
lessons.summary: Emma considers a few places, follows a friend's idea, compares rooms on a website and pays for a week in Canada.
lessons.text:
Emma lived in Denver. She worked in an office, and she had 2 free weeks in August. She wanted to travel, but she did not know where to go.

First, Emma made a list of places to consider. New York was on the list, but it was very hot there in August. Should she consider the south? No, it was hot there too. It was not an easy choice.

Then Emma called her friend Rosa. "What places are you considering?" Rosa asked. Then she suggested Canada. "Go to Vancouver," Rosa said. "It is beautiful in August, and it is not too hot." Rosa also suggested a visit to the parks near the city. Emma liked the idea. Canada was a good choice.

But Emma needed a passport. She did not have one, so she applied for a passport online. She applied in May, and the passport came in June.

Then Emma looked at a travel website. The website had many rooms in Vancouver. She compared the prices. One room was $90 a night. Another room was $150 a night. She also compared the photos and the reviews on the website. The room for $90 was small, but it was near the center of the city.

Emma did not want to spend too much money. She wanted to spend about $1,500 on the whole trip. So she made her choice: the small room near the center. She paid for the room with her credit card. She also paid for her flight with her credit card.

Now everything was ready. Emma was very happy. In August, she was going to Canada!

Questions:
When did Emma have free time?
She had 2 free weeks in August.
Who suggested Canada?
Her friend Rosa suggested Canada.
What did Emma apply for?
She applied for a passport.
What did Emma compare on the website?
She compared the prices, the photos and the reviews.
How much money did Emma want to spend?
She wanted to spend about $1,500.
How did Emma pay for the room?
She paid for the room with her credit card.

lessons.title: Sam Flies Alone
lessons.summary: Sam, 15, flies alone from Chicago to Washington and sends his worried mom a text at every step.
lessons.text:
Sam was 15 years old. He lived in Chicago with his mom. In June, his grandmother asked him to visit her in Washington. His mom could not go with him because she had to work. So Sam had to fly alone.

It was his first time flying alone. His mom was worried. "Don't worry, Mom," Sam said. "I will be safe. I will send you a text before I fly and after I land."

On the day of the trip, his mom drove him to the airport. She was still worried. Sam smiled at her. "Mom, don't worry. I'm 15. I can fly alone."

Before the plane left, Sam sent her a text message: "I'm on the plane. Everything is fine." His mom received the message in the car. She felt a little better.

Sam flew for 2 hours. He was alone, but he was not worried. He read a book and listened to music. Then the plane landed in Washington. Sam sent another text: "I'm in Washington. I'm safe!" His mom received it at her office. She smiled.

His grandmother was waiting for him. She was very happy to see him. Sam took a photo of himself and his grandmother and sent it to his mom. His mom received the photo and wrote back a message: "I'm happy you're safe. Have fun in Washington!"

That night, Sam thought about the day. Flying alone was easy. Next year, he wanted to fly to Washington alone again.

Questions:
Who did Sam visit in Washington?
He visited his grandmother.
Why did Sam fly alone?
His mom had to work.
What did Sam send his mom before the plane left?
He sent her a text message.
How long did Sam fly?
He flew for 2 hours.
What did Sam send his mom after he landed?
He sent her a text: "I'm in Washington. I'm safe!"
What did his mom write back?
She wrote: "I'm happy you're safe. Have fun in Washington!"

lessons.title: A Day in the Capital
lessons.summary: Lin spends a day in Washington: a museum of natural history, original papers from the nation's early days and the building of the highest court.
lessons.text:
Lin was a student from Seattle. In May, she visited Washington for the first time. Washington is the center of the nation's government. Many federal offices are there. Federal means "for the whole nation." Many people in the city work for the federal government.

In the morning, Lin went to a museum of natural history. There she learned about the natural world: rocks, plants and animals. She saw the bones of a huge animal. "These bones are evidence," a sign said. "They are evidence that this animal lived 70 million years ago." Lin looked at the bones for a long time. She wondered how big the animal was. She wondered what it ate.

In the middle of the day, Lin rested in a park in the middle of the city. She ate some food and read about the history of the nation.

After that, she went to a big building with original papers from the early days of the nation. The original papers were very old, and the light in the room was low. On the wall, there was a big image of the first president. Next to it, there was a big image of the papers, so people could read them. Lin wondered about the people who wrote them.

Then Lin walked to the building of the highest court in the nation. There are 9 judges in this court. The judges make decisions on very important cases. Lin stood in front of the building and thought about the judges. She had a thought: "Maybe I can study law. Maybe I can be a judge one day."

That night, Lin wrote to her mother: "Washington is full of history. I love this city."

Questions:
What does "federal" mean?
Federal means "for the whole nation."
Where did Lin go in the morning?
She went to a museum of natural history.
What did the bones show?
They were evidence that the animal lived 70 million years ago.
Where did Lin rest in the middle of the day?
She rested in a park in the middle of the city.
What image was on the wall?
There was an image of the first president.
What thought did Lin have?
She thought: "Maybe I can be a judge one day."

lessons.title: The Train to New York
lessons.summary: Because of a bus strike on Labor Day, Ben takes the train from Union Station to visit his brother in New York.
lessons.text:
Ben lived in Washington. His brother lived in New York. Every year, Ben visited his brother on Labor Day. Labor Day is at the end of the summer. It is a day for working people, and many people do not work on Labor Day.

Ben always went to New York by bus. But this year, the bus drivers were on strike. They wanted more money, so they stopped work. Because of the strike, there were no buses.

So Ben took the train this time. In the morning, he went to Union Station. Union Station is the biggest train station in Washington. It is a beautiful old building.

The station was very full. Many people wanted to take the train because of the strike. Ben got stuck in a long line. He was stuck there for 30 minutes. He was not certain that he could get a seat. But in the end, he got one.

At 10 in the morning, the train pulled into the station. Ben got on the train. A few minutes later, the train pulled out of Union Station.

The ride was 3 hours long. Ben loved the ride. He looked out at small towns, green fields and rivers. He read a book and drank some water. He looked forward to seeing his brother. He also looked forward to the good food in New York.

After 3 hours, the train pulled into a station in New York. His brother was waiting for him.

"How was the ride?" his brother asked.

"It was great," Ben said. "I'm certain of one thing: next year, I will take the train again."

Questions:
Who did Ben visit every year on Labor Day?
He visited his brother in New York.
Why were there no buses?
The bus drivers were on strike.
Where did Ben go in the morning?
He went to Union Station.
How long was Ben stuck in the line?
He was stuck in the line for 30 minutes.
How long was the ride?
The ride was 3 hours long.
What did Ben look forward to?
He looked forward to seeing his brother.

lessons.title: A Room in Chicago
lessons.summary: Kate gets to a small hotel late at night, opens the door with a code and reads a letter from the management about the network and a box of food.
lessons.text:
Kate went to Chicago for work. She got to the city late at night, at 11. She had a room in a small hotel near the center of the city.

At night, there was no one at the front of the hotel. But the hotel sent Kate a code on her phone. The code had 4 numbers. She put the code into the door, and the door opened. Then she used the same code for the door of her room.

The room was small, but it was very clean. Everything in the room was clean. The bed was big and white. On the bed there was a letter from the management.

Kate read the letter. "Thank you for staying with us!" it said. "The management hopes you enjoy your stay." The letter also gave the name of the network and the code for the network. Kate put the network code into her phone, and now her phone was online.

The letter also mentioned a small box in the room. "The box contains water and some food," it said. "It is free." Kate opened the box. It contained water and some food. Kate was very happy, because she did not have time to eat on the way to Chicago.

The letter mentioned one more thing: "We serve food in the morning from 7 to 10."

Kate slept very well that night.

In the morning, Kate wrote a review of the hotel. She mentioned the clean room, the big bed and the free box of food. "The quality of the room is very good," she wrote. "Good quality and a good price." The next day, the management sent her a message: "Thank you, Kate!"

Questions:
How did Kate open the door of the hotel?
She put a code into the door.
What was on the bed?
There was a letter from the management.
What did the letter give?
It gave the name of the network and the code for the network.
What did the box contain?
It contained water and some food.
What did Kate mention in her review?
She mentioned the clean room, the big bed and the free box of food.

lessons.title: Anna Loses Her Voice
lessons.summary: On a trip to Toronto, Anna loses her voice, sees a doctor at a hospital and does exactly what he says.
lessons.text:
Anna was from Boston. She worked at a music school. She usually talked a lot at work, and she usually played music with her students. Her voice was very important for her job.

In March, Anna went to Toronto for a week. The air was very cold there. On her third day, Anna got up and could not speak. She had no voice!

Anna was worried, so she went to a hospital near her hotel. At the front of the hospital, a woman asked for her medical card. "I'm not from Canada," Anna wrote on a piece of paper. "Do you accept my card?" "Yes, we accept it," the woman said. "We also accept credit cards."

There were many patients in the hospital. Anna waited with the other patients for an hour. Then a doctor called her name. He looked at her and asked her some questions. Anna wrote her answers.

"It is not a big problem," he said. "There is no risk to your health, and I can treat it. But there is one risk: if you talk a lot this week, you can lose your voice for a long time."

The doctor treated Anna. Then he gave her a medical paper with a list. "You must protect your voice," he said. "Protect it from the cold air. Drink hot water. Don't talk for 3 days."

Anna did exactly what the doctor said. She drank hot water every hour. She stayed inside and protected her voice from the cold air. She did not talk. When she needed something, she wrote a note.

After 3 days, her voice came back. It was exactly like before. Anna was very happy.

Questions:
What did Anna usually do at work?
She usually talked a lot and played music with her students.
Where did Anna go when she lost her voice?
She went to a hospital near her hotel.
What did the hospital accept?
It accepted her medical card and credit cards.
How long did Anna wait with the other patients?
She waited for an hour.
What did the doctor say about the risk?
He said that if she talked a lot, she could lose her voice for a long time.
What did Anna do?
She did exactly what the doctor said.

lessons.title: The Old Gold Town
lessons.summary: A family visits an old gold town in western Canada, goes into a deep mine and the children look for gold themselves.
lessons.text:
In the summer, Paul and his 2 children, Lily and Max, drove to an old gold town in western Canada. More than 150 years ago, many people came to western Canada to look for gold. They lived in small towns, and they worked very hard.

The town was small and green. There were green fields all around it. The old houses were red, white and green.

First, the family went into an old gold mine. The mine was very deep. It went deep under the ground, and there was very little light inside. A man showed them an old oil lamp. "Long ago, the men in the mine used oil for light," he said. "The oil gave only a little light, so their work was very hard."

Then the man gave the children a challenge. "Can you find gold yourselves?" he asked. He gave each child a box. The box was full of stuff from the old mine: water and small rocks. "Look in this stuff," he said. "Maybe you can find some gold."

Lily made her first attempt. She moved the water and the rocks in her box. She found nothing. She made a second attempt. Nothing again. Max made an attempt too, but he found only small rocks.

"This is a real challenge," Max said.

They did not stop. On her third attempt, Lily saw something very small in the water. It was gold! A few minutes later, Max found a small piece of gold too.

The children were very happy. They found the gold themselves. They put the gold in a small box and took it home.

Questions:
Where was the old gold town?
It was in western Canada.
What was the mine like?
It was very deep, and there was very little light inside.
What did the men in the mine use for light long ago?
They used oil.
What did the man give each child?
He gave each child a box full of stuff from the old mine.
When did Lily find gold?
She found gold on her third attempt.
Who found the gold?
The children found the gold themselves.

lessons.title: A Ball for Ella
lessons.summary: Mark takes his daughter Ella to a major league game in Boston, where she wants to get a ball and finally does.
lessons.text:
Mark had a daughter, Ella. She was 10 years old, and she loved baseball. Ella had a dream: she wanted to see a major league game in Boston.

In June, Mark took his daughter to Boston. Their room was only 6 blocks from the ball park. They walked the 6 blocks to the park. Ella was so happy. Her dream was real!

They got there early. Before the game, the players had training on the field. They threw balls and hit balls. Ella watched the training for a long time. Now she had a new dream: she wanted to get a ball from a real league player.

Ella waited near the field with her hands up. A player threw a ball to the people near her. Ella tried to get the ball, but she failed. A man got it. Then another ball came. Ella tried again, and she failed again.

Mark bought 2 drinks in big paper cups. Ella held her cup and watched the game.

In the middle of the game, a player hit a ball high into the air. The ball came toward Mark and Ella. Ella put down her cup and put up her hands. This time she did not fail. The ball fell into her hands. She finally had a ball!

Everyone around them was happy for her. "I finally have a ball from a major league game!" Ella said.

That night, Mark said, "The day was long, but it was worth it."

"It was worth it," Ella said. "This was the best day of my life."

Questions:
What did Ella want to see?
She wanted to see a major league game in Boston.
How far was their room from the ball park?
It was only 6 blocks from the ball park.
What did the players do before the game?
They had training on the field.
What happened when Ella tried to get a ball before the game?
She failed.
What did Mark buy?
He bought 2 drinks in big paper cups.
When did Ella finally get a ball?
She finally got a ball in the middle of the game.

lessons.title: A Book for Mom
lessons.summary: On her last day in New York, Mia looks for a gift for her mother and buys the big version of a book with color photos of the city.
lessons.text:
Mia visited New York for 4 days. On her last day, she wanted to buy something for her mother. Her mother always said, "Bring me whatever you like. I'm happy with whatever you buy."

Her mother loved New York. It was her favorite city, and she lived there many years ago. Her favorite place in the city was Central Park. So Mia had an idea: a book about New York.

Mia went into a big book shop. There were many books about New York in the shop. Mia found a beautiful book with photos of the city. A man in the shop told her about it. "There are 2 versions of this book," he said. "This is the small version. It has 100 color photos and some black and white photos. The big version has 300 color photos."

"What is the difference in price?" Mia asked.

"The small version is $20, and the big version is $45," the man said. "There is one more difference. The big version also has a chapter about Central Park."

That was exactly the difference Mia wanted. Her mother loved Central Park! "Do you have the big version?" she asked.

"I'm sorry," the man said. "We don't have it here. But we have another shop 3 blocks away. They have the big version there."

Mia walked to the other shop and bought the big version. It was beautiful, but it was very big. It did not fit in her small bag, so she carried it in her hands.

At home, her mother opened the book. She looked at the color photos of Central Park for a long time. "This is perfect," she said.

Questions:
What did her mother always say?
She said, "Bring me whatever you like."
Which place in New York did her mother love?
She loved Central Park.
How many versions of the book were there?
There were 2 versions.
What was the difference between the versions?
The big version had more color photos and a chapter about Central Park.
What did the man say about the big version?
He said, "I'm sorry. We don't have it here."
Why did Mia carry the book in her hands?
It did not fit in her small bag.

lessons.title: A Visit to a Car Plant
lessons.summary: David and his son Leo visit a car plant in Detroit and see how cars are made in its three units.
lessons.text:
David and his son Leo visited Detroit. Detroit is a city of cars. For more than 100 years, car production was at the center of the city's economic life. Many people in Detroit worked in car production, and the economic future of the city was in its cars.

Leo loved cars, so they went on a visit to a big car plant. A plant is a big building where people make things. Ruth was the chief of the plant. The chief showed them around.

"Our plant has 3 units," Ruth said. "Each unit has a different job." In the first unit, machines built the body of each car. The machines performed many jobs very fast. They cut, moved and put together big pieces of the car.

In the second unit, the cars got their color. Some cars were red, and some were blue or black. In the third unit, workers performed the final checks. They checked every door, every light and every window.

"Our technology is very new," Ruth said. "But people are still important. The technology does a lot, but people check everything. Making a good car takes a lot of effort."

On the wall, Leo saw an award. "What is that award for?" he asked.

"Last year, our plant won an award for quality," the chief said. "Every worker made an effort, and every unit did a good job. So we won the award together."

At the end of the visit, Leo sat in a new car. "One day, I want to work here," he said. "I want to make cars too."

Questions:
What was at the center of the economic life of Detroit?
Car production was at the center of its economic life.
Who was Ruth?
She was the chief of the plant.
How many units did the plant have?
The plant had 3 units.
What did the workers in the third unit perform?
They performed the final checks.
What did Ruth say about the technology?
She said the technology was very new, but people were still important.
What award did the plant win?
It won an award for quality.
